rationale: The repository root LICENSE file is a verbatim MIT license text (copyright Max Bachmann 2020-present and Adam Cohen 2011; permission/warranty clauses lines 4-21), confirmed by the declared `license = "MIT"` field in pyproject.toml line 17, by README.md lines 48 and 245-246, and by docs/License.rst lines 6-11 (which literal-includes ../LICENSE). All 49 source files carrying an SPDX identifier use `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` (e.g., src/rapidfuzz/_feature_detector.py line 1). MIT is OSI-approved, permissive, and compatible. LIMITATION: the repo vendors two git submodules (extern/rapidfuzz-cpp and extern/taskflow, pinned in .gitmodules) whose directories are empty/not checked out in this snapshot, so their license texts could not be directly read; they are consumed only via the optional C++ build path (CMakeLists.txt lines 85-142) and the wheel falls back to a pure-Python build when CMake/C++ is unavailable (pyproject.toml lines 59-67). Neither submodule's text could be verified here, but no copyleft/proprietary constraint is present anywhere in the checked-out source, so the aggregate package is permissive.
